title: Crawler Architecture: Visual Guide
outline: 1. From Postings To Fetches | the bridge from IR 101's dictionary-and-postings index to the crawl loop, stepped one stage at a time with sliders for outlinks per page and share already seen | the frontier grows faster than you drain it because each fetch discovers tens of links, and canonicalization must run before the URL-seen test

2. Front And Back Queues | a FIFO frontier versus Mercator's front queues (priority) and back queues (one host each, min-heap on next allowed fetch time), with worker and delay sliders over a 60-second window | what is worth fetching and what may be fetched right now are different questions, and the per-host ceiling of 86,400/delay per day is arithmetic no number of workers can move

3. The robots.txt Rulebook | seven URL paths judged against a real robots.txt by longest matched prefix with Allow winning ties, plus a status-code switch for 200, 404, 5xx and unreachable | the longest match wins rather than the first, and the status semantics are asymmetric: 4xx means crawl freely while 5xx or unreachable means complete disallow, temporarily

4. The Politeness Dial | response time and multiplier k driving the adaptive delay k x t_response with a 1-second floor, overridden by Crawl-delay 10 or 60, with a shared-hosting toggle multiplying load per IP | an adaptive delay protects a struggling server automatically, and Crawl-delay 60 over 2,000,000 pages is 3.8 years, which is a policy problem to solve with a sanctioned bulk channel, not rotating IPs

5. Traps And Canonical Form | faceted-navigation sliders multiplying colour, size, brand, sort and page into unique URLs against 3,000 products, and a canonicalizer toggling nine normalization rules over eight URLs | URL space outruns content space, so per-host budgets and the unique-content-per-URL ratio bound traps, while over-aggressive normalization fails the seen test closed and costs coverage silently
